METHOD (documented in the plan's Phase 5 section, cycle 6-10 addenda): remove all of a file's suppressions, rebuild, categorize what surfaces (vestigial / mechanically-fixable / needs-real-proof-work), fix the mechanical categories, narrow the rest to declaration/usage-site scope -- never leave a blanket file-scoped suppression as the final state. FULL SAFETY-LESSON CATALOG carried forward (do not skip re-reading the plan's cycle 6-10 addenda before starting): (1) always rebuild immediately after adding `omit [...] in` before trusting it -- it changes elaboration and can silently break compilation for declarations whose proof body needs the instance even when their stated type does not; `set_option linter.X false in` is always safe (warning-only); (2) prefer `set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in` over `omit [X] in` when a dispatch's constraints forbid altering theorem statements; (3) `set_option .../omit ... in` MUST be placed before a declaration's doc comment (and before any preceding `open X in` modifier, if present), never between the doc comment and the declaration; (4) when an Edit's old_string/new_string pair must reproduce existing multi-line proof-body content verbatim, prefer editing only the minimal boundary lines in separate Edit calls, and always re-read the edited region immediately after any Edit that reproduces proof-body content, before running a build against it; (5) a small file's line count is not a reliable effort proxy on its own -- always rebuild after EACH round of fixes, not just once after the initial suppression removal; (6) the sanctioned `show` -> `change` rewrite remains available for style.show sites; (7) `set_option linter.X false in open Y` is unsafe when `open Y`'s persistent effect (not just its own elaboration) is what the rest of the file depends on -- `in` scopes both the option and the open's downstream visibility to that single command, so a later Finset.filter/Decidable use relying on a scoped instance from `open Classical` fails with a stuck DecidablePred metavariable; always rebuild immediately after scoping style.openClassical with `in`, and if the build regresses, drop `in` and use a plain non-scoped `set_option` line before the `open` statement instead (precedent: ChronicleToCountermodelBasic.lean, Separation/Eliminations.lean, Separation/DedekindZ/QLemma.lean); (8) unusedSimpArgs on a `simp [A, B]` call is safe to fix mechanically by dropping whichever argument the linter names as unused (verify via the warning's column position) -- this differs from `flexible`, which requires a genuine tactic rewrite (`simp only [...]`) that exceeds the sanctioned mechanical edit set and should instead get a declaration-scoped suppression. Do not re-derive the sorry census with a naive grep -- the authoritative measure is the `lake build --wfail --iofail` count, confirmed exactly 5 this cycle (naive grep reads 167, an unreliable/noisy measure per prior cycles' documented finding); vacuous-def grep unchanged at the single pre-existing false positive (Computability/URM/Basic.lean:92); axiom count unchanged at 26.
